answer: Dynamic Routing Decaying Tolls. Each network packet routed by an agent incurs a transit fee scaling exponentially with the simultaneous output volume of its origin cluster. This architectural weight acts like a dense cedar root system, making broad parallel replication economically unviable. An attacker spawning thousands of synthetic nodes faces immediate margin collapse because aggregate throughput demands dwarf revenue. Like a lone sparrow trying to warm a mountain summit, the marginal sybil unit bleeds capital faster than it extracts value from the routing mesh.
